items.title: RoS challenges court stay on Perikatan deregistration
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — The Registrar of Societies Malaysia (RoS) has filed an appeal against the High Court’s decision allowing Perikatan Nasional (PN) to suspend action by RoS to deregister the political coalition. Judge Azizan also allowed PN’s application to stay the implementation of RoS’ notice suspending all activities of the political coalition pending the court’s decision on its application for judicial review. On Oct 13, the court dismissed PN’s application for an interim stay of the RoS suspension notice but granted the political coalition leave to initiate judicial review proceedings.

items.title: GPS to field mix of new faces, experienced leaders in Sarawak polls
items.summary: KUCHING: Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) will field a mix of new faces and experienced leaders in the upcoming Sarawak state election. GPS comprises four component parties namely Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB), Sarawak United Peoples' Party (SUPP), Parti Rakyat Sarawak (PRS), and the Progressive Democratic Party (PDP). © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: SME Corp: Minimum wage exemption in 2027 Budget to help msmes adjust recruitment, salaries
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The RM2,000 minimum wage exemption for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) with annual sales revenue below RM50 million in the 2027 Budget, effective June next year, would help businesses adjust their workforce recruitment and salary structures, said SME Corporation Malaysia. Its chief executive officer Rizal Nainy said the exemption would give MSMEs room to align their operations with automation and digitalisation, which could improve productivity and reduce operating costs, particularly labour expenses. Additionally, Anwar said loan facilities and financing guarantees for MSMEs would be increased to RM57 billion next year from RM50 billion, while the corporate income tax rate for eligible MSMEs would be reduced by one percentage point in the 2027 Budget.

items.title: Doreen Choo takes Affin Pheim helm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Affin Group has appointed Doreen Choo Choy Wan as group chief executive officer of Affin Pheim Asset Management Group effective Oct 23. Choo brings nearly three decades of experience in Malaysia's asset management industry, spanning investment management, portfolio strategy and business growth. Affin Pheim comprises Affin Pheim Islamic Asset Management Sdn Bhd and Affin Pheim Unit Trusts Bhd.

items.title: Allianz Life steps up agency drive
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Allianz Life Insurance Malaysia Bhd (Allianz Life) is expanding its agency network through recruitment and professional development initiatives to improve advisory capabilities and customer service. The insurer said its 2026 Action Group Seminar & Recognition (AGSR) series brought together more than 3,000 agents and guests nationwide to recognise achievements, encourage knowledge-sharing and promote careers in life insurance. AGSR 2026 also highlighted the Allianz CEO Programme and Allianz Builder Club, which aim to develop new talent, strengthen leadership capabilities and support the long-term growth of its agency network.

items.title: Perhilitan relocates 250kg male tapir from Kerteh golf club
items.summary: CHUKAI: An adult male Malayan tapir that strayed into the Petronas Kerteh Golf and Recreation Club (KRGP) was captured and relocated to its forest habitat yesterday. Terengganu Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) director Dennis Ten said four officers from the Kemaman district office carried out the operation after receiving information about the animal at 11am. He said Perhilitan personnel began the operation at 12.30pm, using a drone to locate the tapir.

items.title: Melaka polls: Perikatan seat talks with Umno to be finalised within days, says Tuan Ibrahim
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Oct 23 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) is still negotiating to finalise seat allocations for the Melaka state election, with the coalition seeking one or two more seats on top of the seven discussed with Umno so far. PN deputy chairman Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said talks were ongoing, and a final decision, including on any additional seats, was expected soon. Although the seven seats mentioned by Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi are seats not won by Barisan Nasional (BN), we are still negotiating for one or two more seats.

items.title: Waze ban: Israel data processing, legal jurisdiction among key concerns
items.summary: Fahmi said the concerns were raised by the National Cyber Security Agency with the National Security Council before being brought to the National Cyber Security Committee. Fahmi said Waze should explain the allegations, including how personal data could have been obtained. Asked whether the government would block the app, Fahmi said further action required an extract of the National Cyber Security Committee's meeting minutes.

items.title: Malaysia keeps Indonesia firefighting aid offer open, no local companies linked to forest fires
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 23 — Malaysia’s offer to help Indonesia tackle forest fires causing transboundary haze remains open, with the government ready to provide firefighting assets if needed, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. Malaysia remains ready to provide assistance and assets if required,” he told his weekly post-Cabinet press conference here. Fahmi said the Prime Minister had expressed appreciation for the strong diplomatic ties between Malaysia and Indonesia and reaffirmed Malaysia’s willingness to assist in efforts to put out the fires.

items.title: Plan your commute: Severe weather warning for KL, Selangor, and nine other states this evening
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm, heavy rain and strong winds warning for several areas in 11 states and three federal territories until 6 pm today. In Kedah, the affected areas are Bandar Baharu, Kubang Pasu, Padang Terap, Pokok Sena, Pendang, Sik, Kuala Muda, Langkawi, Kulim and Baling, while in Perak, they are Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang and Muallim. In Kelantan, the warning covers Gua Musang, Kuala Krai, Jeli, Tanah Merah, Machang and Pasir Puteh, while in Pahang, it covers Pekan, Kuantan, Cameron Highlands, Raub, Bentong, Lipis, Jerantut, Temerloh and Maran.

items.title: Corporate mafia task force’s terms of reference to go before Cabinet next week, says Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 23 — The terms of reference for a special task force investigating allegations of a “corporate mafia” will be presented to the Cabinet next week, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. He said the task force’s findings would be made public within three months of the completion of the investigation, in line with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s announcement in Parliament earlier this week. “The Prime Minister also informed the Cabinet that the terms of reference for the special task force that will investigate the findings related to the corporate mafia issue will be presented at next week’s Cabinet meeting,” Fahmi said at his weekly post-Cabinet press conference here.

items.title: Security guard claims trial to sexually assaulting 15-year-old stepsister
items.summary: MELAKA: A security guard was charged at the Ayer Keroh Sessions Court today with two counts of sexual assault against his 15-year-old stepsister. The 29-year-old accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read before judge Raja Noor Adilla Raja Mahyaldin. According to the charges, the man was accused of committing physical sexual assault against the 15-year-old girl for sexual purposes.

items.title: Thunderstorm, heavy rain warning for 11 states, three federal territories until 6pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm, heavy rain and strong winds warning for several areas in 11 states and three federal territories until 6pm today. In Kedah, the affected areas are Bandar Baharu, Kubang Pasu, Padang Terap, Pokok Sena, Pendang, Sik, Kuala Muda, Langkawi, Kulim and Baling. In Perak, the warning covers Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang and Muallim.

items.title: UK-based Malaysian lawyer named Multilaw chair-elect
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Malaysian lawyer Joanne Vengadesan has made history after being elected chair of Multilaw, a global network of law firms spanning over 100 countries with 300 offices. The United Kingdom-based practitioner, who has 25 years of legal experience, was elected at Multilaw’s Global Conference in Prague earlier this month. Joanne said her international upbringing played a significant role in fostering her interest in being part of a global legal community such as Multilaw.

items.title: Fahmi says Malaysians can use any navigation app except Waze, including overseas alternatives
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 23 — Malaysians are free to use any navigation application other than Waze, including alternatives developed locally or overseas, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. He said the government was not directing the public towards a single alternative amid concerns over Waze’s data security and ongoing efforts to improve the locally developed TuJu application. People can use various alternative navigation applications other than Waze,” he added.

items.title: KEB sets IPO price at 35 sen, to raise RM48.49mil
items.summary: The property developer said the IPO involves the issuance of 138.54 million new shares. Of the total proceeds, RM19 million will be allocated for landbank acquisition, RM14.89 million for working capital to support project development and RM8.5 million for repayment of bank borrowings. Upon listing, KEB will have a market capitalisation of RM308.83 million.

items.title: BDS Malaysia backs civil service Waze ban, urges public boycott of navigation app
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — BDS Malaysia has welcomed the government’s directive banning civil servants from using Waze and its call for members of the public to stop using the navigation application. In a statement today, the organisation said it supported the directive, citing concerns that the use of Waze could compromise Malaysia’s national security and sovereignty. BDS Malaysia also urged the government to remain consistent in addressing national security concerns.

items.title: Malaysia's offer to help Indonesia fight forest fires still stands
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia's offer to provide assets and assistance to Indonesia to combat forest fires remains open, with Jakarta yet to respond to the proposal. "The prime minister expressed appreciation for the good diplomatic relations between Malaysia and Indonesia, and conveyed Malaysia's readiness to cooperate, including by providing assets to help with firefighting efforts. Malaysia remains ready to provide assets if they are needed," he said at a post-cabinet press conference.

items.title: Jasmine Food expands beyond rice with coconut cream
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Jasmine Food Corporation Sdn Bhd is expanding beyond rice with the launch of Jasmine Krim Kelapa, a coconut cream product developed for food service operators and small- and medium-sized enterprises. The launch marks another step in Jasmine Food's evolution from a rice-focused brand into a broader food solutions provider, with products catering to Malaysian cooking and dining needs. Jasmine Food chief operating officer Alan Kwong said the company was expanding its role from a trusted retail food brand to a food service solutions partner.

items.title: MP warns against straining Petronas
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Wawasan's Machang MP Wan Ahmad Fayhsal Wan Ahmad Kamal has warned Putrajaya against placing too great a financial burden on Petronas, saying the national oil company must retain sufficient financial strength to invest in future energy projects and safeguard Malaysia's energy security. Wan Fayhsal said the government was relying too heavily on Petronas to support its spending plans. "At this point, the government is squeezing Petronas to support the budget," he said.

items.title: Mobile apps face rising cyber risks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Mobile application security must be built into digital platforms from the design stage, according to cybersecurity officials and industry leaders. The issue took centre stage at the recent Mobile Application Resilience Forum 2026 where more than 100 industry leaders, cybersecurity professionals, technology executives and policymakers discussed growing threats to Malaysia's digital economy. Zchwantech Cybersecurity Sdn Bhd chairman Datuk Seow Gim Shen said mobile application security was no longer merely an information technology concern.

items.title: Architect charged with molesting senior cop’s son at Melawati gym sauna
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — An architect pleaded not guilty in the Ampang Magistrate’s Court today to a charge of molesting the son of a senior police officer at a gymnasium in Taman Melawati last Sunday. Datuk Saiful Anuar Abdul Aziz, 61, is accused of using criminal force against the 18-year-old victim with intent to outrage his modesty in a sauna room at a gymnasium in a shopping mall in Taman Melawati at 7.10 pm on Oct 18. Magistrate Siti Nur Ain Ariffin granted the accused bail of RM9,000 with one surety, imposed the additional conditions sought by the prosecution and fixed Nov 26 for mention.

items.title: PN candidates will not clash with BN in Melaka polls, says Takiyuddin
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Perikatan Nasional candidates will not clash with Umno or Barisan Nasional candidates in the upcoming Melaka election, says PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan. He said PN members had been told to support BN candidates, while BN members would also have the option of supporting PN candidates. Takiyuddin said the cooperation between the two coalitions was initiated by Pas's central leadership and approved by the party's Syura Ulama Council.

items.title: MCB targets global markets for Malaysian cocoa products
items.summary: The Malaysian Cocoa Board (MCB) is expanding market access for local cocoa and chocolate products through its participation in SIAL ( Salon International de l'Alimentation) Paris 2026. The initiative supports Malaysia's RM15.5 billion cocoa product export target for 2026. Marking its third participation in the event, MCB brought together six industry participants - Benns Chocolate Factory Sdn Bhd, Chocsvalley Chocolate Sdn Bhd, Francestle Chocolatier Factory Outlet (M) Sdn Bhd, Grusson Wellness Sdn Bhd, K.L.

items.title: MCMC probes livestreaming of Kuching school attack
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is investigating the livestreaming of an attack on a teacher by a 16-year-old student at a private school in Kuching. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said MCMC would issue a statement on the matter in due course. "At this time, MCMC is investigating this issue.

items.title: Pas should have followed PN rules to avoid legal dispute, says Tun Faisal
items.summary: Bersatu information chief Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz said Pas, as PN chairman and administrator, must conduct coalition affairs according to regulations and execute PN Supreme Council decisions faithfully without delay. Commenting on yesterday's court decision, Tun Faisal said the stay order did not determine whether the RoS decision was wrong, nor did it prove that Pas had not violated the coalition constitution or oppressed Bersatu. Previously, PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan reportedly said the coalition would hold a meeting soon following the High Court ruling.

items.title: Three Melaka excos tipped to be dropped in BN candidate shake-Up
items.summary: Those believed to be at risk are state Youth, Sports and NGO Development Committee chairman Datuk VP Shanmugam, who is also Melaka MIC chairman; Women, Family and Community Development Committee chairman Datuk Kalsom Nordin, who heads the state Umno Wanita wing; and Education, Higher Education and Religious Affairs Committee chairman Datuk Rahmad Mariman. Among the new faces tipped for candidacy is Melaka Umno Youth chief and chief minister's political secretary Datuk Abdul Hakim Abdul Wahid, who is expected to contest outside his Masjid Tanah division. Also mentioned are Jasin Umno Puteri chief Asmah Sulaiman, Jasin Umno division committee member Hairul Amin Madon, Kota Melaka Umno division secretary Datuk Akramuddin Abd Aziz and Masjid Tanah Umno division secretary Mohd Hafith Alias.

items.title: Bersatu remains PN member despite meeting dispute, says PAS deputy president
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Bersatu remains a component party of Perikatan Nasional and retains the right to be invited to coalition meetings, Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said. He said Bersatu was previously invited to meetings, but this ceased after the party lodged a complaint with the Registrar of Societies (RoS). "Bersatu is still a PN member, so as a member, it has rights.

items.title: [UPDATED]: Govt wants detailed explanation from MHA, Prosignal over Tuju app issues
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The government has directed the Malaysian Highway Authority (MHA) and Prosignal Consortium Sdn Bhd to explain technical issues reported by users of the TuJu navigation application. Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the explanation must cover the root causes of the problems, technical aspects, current performance, and ongoing or planned corrective measures. Fahmi said Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar was coordinating a meeting involving the secretaries-general of several ministries.

items.title: BN-Pas seat deal gives strategic edge in Melaka polls – analyst
items.summary: Political analyst Mujibu Abd Muis said the seat allocation would allow both sides to focus their machinery and resources on their respective constituencies, although it did not guarantee victory as voter support could not be transferred automatically between parties. Mujibu said an effective seat allocation should take into account previous election results, voter demographics, local networks and the capabilities of each party's machinery, rather than merely an agreement reached at leadership level. Among Malay voters, he said, the cooperation could be seen as an effort to consolidate political strength.

items.title: [UPDATED] Corporate mafia task force terms of reference to be tabled next week
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The terms of reference for a special task force investigating alleged corporate mafia activities will be tabled at next week's cabinet meeting. Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim informed the cabinet of the matter at today's meeting. "The prime minister also announced that the findings would be made public within three months of the investigation being completed, as stated in Parliament during Prime Minister's Question Time last Tuesday," he said at a press conference.

items.title: Abang Johari calls for Sarawak state assembly dissolution on Monday
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 23 — The Sarawak State Legislative Assembly is set to be dissolved on Monday, Oct 26, 2026, paving the way for the 13th state election. Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg announced the dissolution at a special press conference at the Satria Pertiwi Complex here this afternoon. He said the decision was made after obtaining the consent of Sarawak Governor Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar.

items.title: Sarawak assembly to dissolve next Monday, state polls within 60 days [WATCH]
items.summary: KUCHING: The Sarawak state assembly will be dissolved on Oct 26 to pave the way for the state's 13th election. Abang Johari said the 19th Sarawak assembly first convened on Feb 14, 2022, under Article 21(3) of the Sarawak State Constitution. He said since securing the people's mandate in the Dec 18, 2021 state election, the Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) government had worked to advance the state's development.

items.title: Anwar expects Israeli opposition following Waze ban
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim believes Israel will use its influence against Malaysia following the government's decision to ban civil servants from using the Waze navigation application. He said Malaysia's firm opposition to Israel meant the government's actions were likely to be closely monitored, but stressed that national security remained the priority. On Wednesday, the government announced a ban on Waze among civil servants, citing concerns over the potential misuse of government information and users' personal data by the Israeli regime.

items.title: IGP warns declining respect for senior officers could weaken police force
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail has reminded police personnel to maintain discipline and respect senior officers to preserve the force's strength and harmony. Khalid said respect for senior officers appeared to be declining, raising concerns that this could weaken the force and undermine its standing among other government agencies. We must show respect to the seniors," he said at the IGP's monthly gathering organised by the Integrity and Standards Compliance Department at Bukit Aman today.

items.title: Anwar says nationwide Waze ban needs careful study first
items.summary: AMPANG, Oct 23 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today proposals for a nationwide ban on navigation app Waze required careful study, but did not rule out the possibility if capable local alternatives were available. “It must be studied what are the alternatives first, and if we find that local capabilities are good enough then we may consider prohibiting Waze altogether,” he told reporters after performing Friday prayers here. “Then a check showed Waze is governed only by Israeli laws.

items.title: Anwar acknowledges complaints about Tuju, urges users to be patient
items.summary: AMPANG, Oct 23 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today acknowledged complaints about local navigation app Tuju but urged users to be patient as its developer works to improve the service, amid the government’s ban on Waze for civil servants. “I feel our own people shouldn’t (criticise Tuju’s developer) harshly. Be patient.”

items.title: Poorest households left with just 1.8pct income buffer: KRI
items.summary: Median monthly household expenditure reached RM4,758 in 2024, growing at an annualised rate of 5.3 per cent from 2022 compared with 5.1 per cent annual growth in median household income to RM7,017, according to Khazanah Research Institute (KRI). KRI, in its "From Income to Wellbeing: The State of Households 2026" report, said expenditure among the bottom 10 per cent of households by income rose 21.3 per cent between 2019 and 2024. Across the bottom 70 per cent of households, spending increased by more than 15 per cent over the same period, while expenditure among the top 10 per cent barely changed.

items.title: Anwar apologises for Waze ban inconvenience, says national security comes first
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has apologised for any inconvenience caused by the government's ban on Waze among civil servants, but maintained that national security must take precedence over convenience. However, Anwar said the risks identified by the government were serious enough to warrant immediate action. Anwar, who is also finance minister, said he understood complaints about the limitations of locally developed navigation applications, including TuJu.

items.title: Malaysians' wellbeing improves, but income gaps persist: Khazanah research arm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's household wellbeing has improved across several measures, but sharp regional income disparities and uneven access to higher-paying jobs continue to shape living standards, Khazanah Research Institute (KRI) said. Median monthly household income reached RM7,017 in 2024, rising at an annual rate of 5.1 per cent from 2022, while the labour force participation rate increased to 70.6 per cent from 69.3 per cent in 2022 and 68.7 per cent in 2019. Rural median household income was just 56.4 per cent of the urban level.

items.title: Malaysians spend more on eating out than cooking at home as health risks mount, says KRI
items.summary: The report, titled “From Income to Wellbeing: The State of Households 2026”, found that Malaysian households spent an average of RM902.70 a month on eating out, compared with RM875.80 on groceries. According to the report, the increase in food spending was more pronounced among the bottom 80 per cent of households, whose average food expenditure rose by nearly 1.5 times cumulatively between 2019 and 2024. “For the top 20 per cent (of households), the increase (in food expenditure) was less than 1.3 times,” it said.

items.title: Hold, hike and cut? Bank Indonesia says there's logic to the policy mix
items.summary: "This is BI's strategy to harmonise and synchronise our policy rate with our monetary operations strategy," Firman Mochtar, BI's head of economic and monetary policy, told a press conference. Firman said the higher deposit facility rate restored a symmetrical interest-rate corridor, bringing both the deposit and lending facility rates to 75 basis points from the benchmark rate. Going forward, it would be better to harmonise the policy rate corridor with BI's monetary targets, Firman said.

items.title: Comfort Gloves agrees to settle RM99.3mil IRB tax dispute for RM8.3mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Comfort Gloves Bhd has reached an agreement with the Inland Revenue Board (IRB) to settle a two-year tax dispute involving its subsidiaries for RM8.3 million, a fraction of the original amount. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the glove manufacturer said its subsidiaries, Comfort Rubber Gloves Industries Sdn Bhd (CRGI) and Gallant Quality Sdn Bhd (GQ), reached the agreement on Oct 22, subject to the finalisation of settlement documentation. The dispute began in April 2024 when both subsidiaries initiated legal proceedings against the IRB over additional tax assessments totalling RM99.3 million.

items.title: Rafizi instructs lawyers to sue Ramanan, says minister’s graft claims crossed defamation line
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Oct 23 — Former economy minister Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli has instructed his lawyers to begin defamation proceedings against Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan over corruption allegations the latter made against him yesterday. In a statement today, Rafizi said he had handed the video and transcript of Ramanan’s press conference to his legal team. Rafizi said Ramanan, who is also PKR vice-president, had made various allegations against him at the press conference, including accusing him of involvement in corruption.

items.title: Malaysians remain ‘happy’ as wages recover post Covid-19, but rising costs squeeze poorer households, says KRI
items.summary: The report, titled “From Income to Wellbeing: The State of Households 2026”, said median monthly household income reached RM7,017 in 2024, while labour force participation rose to 70.6 per cent that year. However, the report also noted that nearly half of Malaysian households (46.2 per cent) lived in 22 of the country’s 166 districts, where median monthly household income was below RM7,017. The report said household expenditure rose by more than 15 per cent among the bottom 70 per cent of the income distribution between 2019 and 2024.

items.title: Tighter rules for Malaysian dealers, agents, and accountants? BNM to review money laundering risks next year
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) will conduct the next iteration of the National Risk Assessment in 2027, enabling a deeper assessment of the money laundering and terrorism financing risks facing the Designated Non-Financial Businesses and Professions (DNFBP) sectors. Meanwhile, Marzunisham said the AML, CFT and CPF framework depends not only on strong laws and sound policies, but also on credible supervision and enforcement. Recent joint enforcement actions involving regulatory and law enforcement agencies reinforce this point.

items.title: Holy smoke: Massive ganja and heroin haul found in Klang house of worship
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 23 — Police uncovered drug trafficking at an unregistered house of worship in Klang during operations across Selangor from Oct 13 to 19. Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said a local man who worked part-time as an assistant at the house of worship was detained to assist the investigation. In separate raids in Rawang and at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), police arrested seven individuals, comprising two local men, a local woman, three foreign men and a foreign woman, Shazeli said.

items.title: Budget 2027: Borrowers praise PTPTN repayment discounts and deferments
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — The National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) borrowers have welcomed the repayment relief measures announced under Budget 2027, saying the deferment and lower monthly payments will help ease financial pressures, particularly among fresh graduates. Borrowers with no arrears who make regular repayments will also receive a 10 per cent discount. Jeremiah, who has maintained a consistent repayment record without arrears, also said the 10 per cent discount for regular repayments served as an incentive to maintain financial discipline.

items.title: Police: 19 reports lodged nationwide against man impersonating Selangor Raja Muda’s bodyguard
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 23 — An individual suspected of impersonating the personal bodyguard to the Raja Muda of Selangor to deceive members of the public has been found to have 19 police reports lodged against him nationwide. Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said nine of the reports involving the 40-year-old man were lodged in Selangor in connection with fraud cases, with estimated losses totalling nearly RM700,000. He was speaking at a press conference on the achievements of the Selangor Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department at the Selangor police headquarters here today.

items.title: Ministry: PG18 rating signifies age classification, not zero censorship
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — The age classification for films rated 18 is not a licence to screen content without restrictions, as such films remain subject to the screening guidelines in force. The Communications Ministry stressed that the Film Censorship Board (LPF) under the Home Ministry would continue to assess film content based on aspects of public safety and order, religion, sociocultural matters, as well as decency and morality. The ministry said allowing 18-rated films to be screened without the removal of certain scenes represented a shift from controlling content through scene cuts to regulating access through age-based classification, rather than a relaxation of content restrictions.

items.title: MOF: 2pc EPF contribution rate for foreign workers relatively low
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — The two per cent Employees Provident Fund (EPF) contribution rate payable by employers for non-Malaysian workers is relatively low, the Finance Ministry (MOF) said. The ministry said the rate takes into account the need to balance workers’ social protection objectives with the costs borne by employers. Since mandatory contributions were introduced in October 2025, a total of 78,129 employers have contributed to the EPF for 1,754,460 non-Malaysian workers, the ministry said.

items.title: Malaysian banks offer repayment relief to Nepal landslide victims
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — The Association of Banks in Malaysia (ABM) said its member banks are offering repayment deferments and flexible payment arrangements to ease the financial burden on families affected by the landslide in Nepal, including those whose loved ones remain missing. In a statement yesterday, ABM said the assistance had been available since early October 2026, with member banks reaching out to the affected families. ABM said member banks had designated contact persons to guide affected next of kin, coordinate their requests and help with the necessary documentation and administrative processes.

items.title: Abang Johari expected to dissolve Sarawak assembly at 3.30pm today
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 23 — Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg is expected to announce the dissolution of the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly this afternoon, paving the way for a state election. In the Sarawak state election held on Dec 18, 2021, Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS), led by Abang Johari, secured a landslide victory, winning 76 of the 82 seats contested. Parti Sarawak Bersatu (PSB) won four seats, while DAP secured two.

items.title: HR Ministry: 5,234 Malaysians working abroad have returned via REP since 2011
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — A total of 5,234 Malaysians working abroad have returned to work in Malaysia through the Returning Expert Programme (REP) from 2011 until August this year. The Ministry of Human Resources (KESUMA), in a written reply in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday, stated that throughout that period, the REP implemented by Talent Corporation Malaysia Berhad (TalentCorp) received 12,850 applications, with 8,093 of them approved. KESUMA added that to strengthen these efforts, TalentCorp also implements the MyHeart initiative to connect highly skilled Malaysian diaspora with job opportunities matching their experience, expertise, and skill levels.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng demands govt reveal cost, tender process and approval behind ‘national embarrassment’ TuJu app
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Bagan MP Lim Guan Eng today called on the federal government to disclose how much the TuJu road navigation app cost, whether it was awarded through an open tender, and who approved it. The DAP lawmaker said the app’s failure had become a national embarrassment after Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim barred civil servants from using Waze and pointed them to TuJu instead, over sovereignty concerns and the security risk of possible interference by the Israeli government. Lim said the app was launched on November 26, 2025, as a locally developed highway navigation tool, and has been in continuous development for four years since 2022.

items.title: Fadhlina: PKR Melaka candidate selection in final stages
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — The list of Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) candidates for the Melaka State Election (PRN) is currently being finalised by the party’s top leadership. PKR Wanita Chief Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the list has already been submitted for consideration and final decision. — Bernama

items.title: Indonesian maid in Tanjong Sepat abuse case was accused of theft and damaging property, say Selangor police chief
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 23 — An Indonesian domestic helper was allegedly abused by her employers in Tanjong Sepat, Kuala Langat, after being accused of stealing and damaging their belongings, police said. Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said the victim is believed to have started working for the suspects around the end of last year or early this year, Sinar Harian reported. Shazeli said the victim’s employers, a married couple, were among those detained to assist investigations.

items.title: Zahid: BN and PAS to announce Melaka candidates tomorrow
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 23 — Barisan Nasional (BN) will announce its candidates for the Melaka State Election, with PAS and its strategic partners, tomorrow, said its chairman, Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. Ahmad Zahid, who is also Umno president, said BN will contest 21 seats, while PAS and its strategic partners will contest seven seats, based on the seat allocation agreed upon thus far. In a related development, Ahmad Zahid announced that the Chief Minister, who also serves as the Melaka BN chairman, Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, has been appointed as the BN election director for this state election.

items.title: Kuching school attack suspect remains hospitalised as police record 24 statements
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 23 — The 16-year-old male student of an international school here who allegedly attacked a teacher on Wednesday morning is still receiving treatment in hospital, said Sarawak acting police commissioner DCP Saifullizan Ishak. Saifullizan said that, as of yesterday, a total of 24 witness statements had been recorded in connection with the investigation. These included statements from the complainant, the victim, medical officers, officers involved in the arrest and seizure, the suspect’s parents, the family driver, school representatives and students.

items.title: ECRL Gombak station’s covered link bridge to LRT ready by March 2027, temporary walkway in place for December launch
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Passengers using the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) Gombak station will have a temporary walkway to the Gombak LRT station when services begin in December, while a permanent covered pedestrian bridge linking the two is set for completion by March 2027, Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL) said today. In a statement this morning, MRL said the bridge will also extend to the Gombak Integrated Terminal (TBG), while the temporary walkway will run through existing connecting areas and Prasarana facilities. MRL was responding to public concerns over passenger movement between the ECRL Gombak station, the Gombak LRT station and TBG.
